thread:
mike: quick idea  add a prewarm "lease" at the gateway so clients can ask the edge to warm upstream conns / caches before sending short, latency-sensitive requests. thoughts?
anya: sounds useful for p99 on read-heavy routes. must be opt-in per-route and limited per-tenant.
sven: agree. safety: prewarm should never do irreversible work by default. restrict to safe methods or require explicit idempotency token.
tia: handshake sketch: client sends `x-rw-prefetch:intent=1`; gateway responds with `103 Prefetch-Lease: id=abc; ttl=400` while it warms. client includes `x-rw-lease: abc` on real request. upstream can honor or ignore.
anya: hedging + retries: lease binding helps. first effective lease wins; other attempts get `prefetch-status: ignored`. prewarm must be cancellable if hedged request loses.
ate infra-bot: canary note: prewarm v0.1 -> canary 10% on /v1/fast. observed cold p95 -110ms, upstream conn delta +9%.
mike: action items: I'll write an RFC sketch with header list, tia write hedging notes, sven add idempotency rules. target RFC by EOW.
anya: also track metrics: prewarm_requests, prewarm_accept_rate, prewarm_memory_delta, prewarm_cost_ms.
mit infra-bot: RFC created: https://rfc.internal/r/3098-gateway-prefetch-lease
